historicalAssessment.assessment: Both funeral examples and nested Bao-yu quotations are complete. Screening the women and asking that the used cup be washed are not recast as courtship. San-jie’s own observation and Er-jie’s teasing inference remain separate; repaired nested quotation is respected.

Joker’s marriage forecast is quoted speculation. Two or three years, leaving in three to five days and the half-month outward-and-return journey are kept distinct. Long-er’s old lady is Old Mrs You in the immediate household, not a new Jia-family presence.
Early retirement does not erase the night spent questioning. Jia Lian arrives only the following afternoon; Er-jie urges him not to neglect his work.

Departure after month-end and half-month absence remain Jia Lian’s plan. Er-jie’s insistence on her sister’s reform and constancy is neither narrator certification of every past claim nor a reversal of agency.

One- and ten-year vows, conditional religious withdrawal if Liu is dead, five-year-old birthday performance and last year’s report remain distinct. Grandmother is a defensible contextual reading of the elder visited with Mother, not Old Mrs You herself. Liu is an amateur young-male-lead performer.

Cold face/heart, affection for Bao-yu, the Xue blockhead epithet and uncertain return are Jia Lian’s speech. Drift-like-duckweed and possible years of waiting keep the uncertainty; Er-jie defends her sister’s determination.

San-jie chooses Liu for herself, distinguishes present religious discipline from the emphatic hundred-year vow and breaks one jade pin into two pieces. Speech, act, subsequent conduct and separate enquiries retain their order. Tealeaf does not certify a return.

Neighbour enquiry, report to Er-jie, false early departure, two concealed nights and actual departure remain separate. The sisters’ changed domestic conduct is narrated without an invented reconciliation.

Three days on the road, travelling routines, pack train and about ten mounted masters and servants are intact. Liu and Xue are recognized together before the inn conversation; the reconciliation has not been prematurely explained.

Xue reports departure for home in spring, recent robbery, rescue of both lives and goods, refused thanks and sworn brotherhood. Two hundred li south leads to the aunt; a home and marriage are promises. Jia Lian conceals San-jie’s initiative explicitly.

Secrecy until a son is born is Jia Lian’s instruction, not an actual birth. Xue’s cousin complaint and Liu’s restraint are preserved. Beauty preference, gracious submission, aunt visit, unnamed mid-month plan and Jia Lian’s concern follow the protected P004 passage.

All protected P004 courtesies and pledge conditions are present. The ordinary defensive sword stays with Liu; a different heirloom pair is offered without importing another edition’s explicit transfer act. Both proverb lines stand after the parting; military commissioner remains the local office.

The tenth-month return is an order, not elapsed time. Next-day homeward departure precedes domestic backfill. The repaired lonely-coverlet reading, resolve, attention to mother/sister and sexual loneliness remain. Means-allowed is defensible on lexical check. Ornament is descriptive, not an archaeological reconstruction.

Two separate male/female inscriptions, cold bright autumn-water simile, keeping and hanging the pair, daily reassurance and Jia Lian’s further two days are intact. English makes the inscription meanings intelligible without selecting a reader note.
Xi-feng’s improvement, Jia Zhen’s new companion and loss of interest remain distinct. Another thirty taels comes from Jia Zhen for the trousseau, not from the earlier Xue promise.

Only in the eighth month does Liu arrive. Aunt Xue, Xue Ke and sick Xue Pan remain separate people. Travel hardship, illness, doctor and thanks keep local causal order; forgiveness of the old affair is not universal absolution.

Prepared wedding supplies precede next-day visit to Bao-yu. Bao-yu has heard but not witnessed the secret marriage. His beauty praise prompts Liu’s suspicion, with Liu himself explaining the hasty pledge and lack of closeness.

Liu’s enquiry, Bao-yu’s one-month acquaintance, two stepsisters and You/you-wu sound bridge are complete. Ning mansion’s cats, dogs, two clean stone lions and the coarse cuckold/leavings slur stay Liu’s accusation. Bao-yu’s flush, apology and smiling rebuff preserve the turn.

Perhaps even I am not clean extends Bao-yu’s rebuff. Liu apologizes for forgetting himself; Bao-yu’s deliberate rejoinder retains its sting. Illness and hot-headedness are two distinct reasons not to consult Xue Pan before demanding the pledge.

Liu’s distant Aunt/your-junior courtesies precede the aunt’s fourth-month engagement story, which stays his stated excuse. Gold/silk is hypothetical; grandfather’s swords are actual claimed heirlooms. Jia Lian’s pledge wordplay and objection retain force.

Reconsideration, willingness to accept blame, categorical refusal and proposed move outside remain distinct speech acts. Formal diction fits the rupture without turning it into a modern legal negotiation.

San-jie’s overhearing, interpretation of his contempt, anticipated humiliation and sudden act follow the source order. Female blade concealed/right hand, remaining sword with scabbard/left hand are consistent. Both elegiac lines, attempted rescue, mother’s curse and Er-jie’s intervention are complete. Er-jie’s causality claim remains hers.

Er-jie warns of scandal; Jia Lian releases Liu. Liu’s late brave-and-virtuous-wife praise is his remorse, not evidence of a completed marriage. Body grief, coffin purchase, witnessed encoffining and renewed coffin grief retain their sequence.

Dazed wandering leads into an apparently real page/new-house scene without advance dream labelling. Sword pair and book/register object, five years of love, Disenchantment’s commission, love-root repetitions and final repudiation remain. Scroll follows the current bounded guidance; no contents are invented.

Uncertain awakening reveals absence of page/house only now. Ruined temple, unnamed cross-legged louse-catching Taoist, paradoxical answer, bone-cold recognition, male-blade tonsure and unknown departure are complete. Ten thousand hair/attachment image and closing formula remain.

historicalAssessment.judgment: Both seeing/hearing causes and homesickness/interrogation results survive; Dai-yu resolves Pin-qing without inventing a person. Three-line title is parallel and unobtrusive.

Burial outside the city, grief of the named family, Xiang-lian’s attachment, the Taoist’s cold intervention, cutting hair and unknown departure all remain. Opening recap is not a second death or conversion.

Aunt Xue’s projected house/furnishings/wedding are intentions interrupted by overheard death news. Bao-chai’s explicit failure to take it to heart is retained without enlarging it into a diagnosis. Her proverb and former-life explanation remain her speech.
Bao-chai turns from deaths to business and courtesy. Ten/twenty days and several months both remain, despite their tension; no alternate chapter itinerary has been substituted.

Xue Pan enters still tearful and asks about both people; Aunt Xue asks about the renunciation and urges a search. Her account of his lack of parents/brothers is attributed, not new biographical narration.

Aunt Xue’s nearby-temple supposition, Xue Pan’s unsuccessful search, her possible-good-outcome consolation, wedding preparations and homely slow-bird proverb keep their distinct force. More than half a month is not harmonized.
Two/three thousand li, four/five months and the proposed invitations survive. Xue Pan’s frustrated self-excuse remains colloquial and does not cancel his actual grief.

Mr Zhang reports two private-purchase trunks outside trade accounts; yesterday’s completed dispatch explains today’s arrival. Two additional carriers, palm-fibre covers and protective boards are retained; Bao-chai’s teasing ten/twenty days and hypothetical year end remain.

Every nested gift category is represented, including mercury tumblers, sand lamps, staged clay figures under green gauze and the separate Xue Pan likeness. No clockwork, lacquer, produce or invented material specification is added.
Bao-chai inspects the portrait rather than treating all gifts alike. Oriole takes the trunk with several old women; Aunt Xue separately dispatches Tong-xi to Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang and others.

Bao-chai retains her own share, differentiates parcel categories and both differentiates and doubles Dai-yu’s portion. Oriole travels with one old woman. Hair oil and scented pendants are not dropped merely because not in the earlier trunk list.

Dai-yu’s loss of both parents, lack of brothers and dependence on relatives ground the grief. Nightingale knows but speaks indirectly through gratitude, health and the elders’ care; no motive is invented for Bao-chai.
Nightingale’s blood/vital-energy explanation remains period character speech. Concern for Dai-yu and for Grandmother Jia is retained; the maid announces Master Bao and Nightingale invites him in.
Dai-yu’s forced smile and denial differ from Bao-yu’s concern. Nightingale signals towards the table behind the bed; Bao-yu recognizes Bao-chai’s gifts and teases about a shop, not actual trade.

Bao-yu knowingly avoids the true grief and makes the two-boatloads-next-year joke. Dai-yu recognizes the kindness without accepting his false premise; the two/three-year-old comparison and refusal of pettiness remain.

Bao-yu’s deliberate object-by-object chatter, closeness at the bed and Dai-yu’s reluctant response remain. Hearing southern sights is a substitute for homecoming, not a planned voyage. Her reddened eyes close the scene without extra sentiment.

Dai-yu leaves with Bao-yu, then narration turns back to the dinner. Four partners attend next day, wine is served and Aunt Xue sends greetings. Two missing guests and Jia Lian’s further Ping-an Zhou departure remain local reported chronology.

Reverend Liu is Xue Pan’s sardonic relabelling, not a new office. The partners’ hearsay about wind and their alternate sorcery explanation stay expressly uncertain. No invented encounter is certified.

Xue Pan’s complaint, exhaustive failed search and admission that he cried lead to an unusually listless dinner. The few cups and early dispersal preserve embarrassment rather than making him comic throughout.
The gift recipients arrive to thank Bao-chai; his courteous attempt to decline contrasts with her modest account of the local curiosities. No economic value is invented.

The precious-away-from-home proverb touches Dai-yu’s feelings, prompting Bao-yu’s diversion. Dai-yu’s sharp rejoinder lets the three laugh; Bao-chai’s walking advice remains personal speech rather than medical narration.
Bao-chai explains her own recent bodily discomfort and occupation as distraction; Dai-yu agrees. The return to Naiad’s House preserves place identity and closes the visit.

Aunt Zhao’s delight, claim of apparent equal treatment, comparison with Dai-yu and calculated visit to Lady Wang are correctly assigned to her mind and speech. The narrator does not endorse her fairness claim against the known doubled share.

Lady Wang recognizes and coolly dismisses the overture; Aunt Zhao suppresses anger before leaving and then flings the gifts aside. Optional O01 improves the unfamiliar nose/dust idiom; no missing event or mandatory fidelity correction.

Aroma’s admonition ends before her walk to Xi-feng. The thief complaint is acceptable figurative grievance, not admission of theft. Deliberately louder footsteps announce her tactfully; Xi-feng’s staged repose and courteous greeting do not erase prior anger.

Xi-feng summons Wang-er and separately questions Patience’s information source. The next unit continues Patience’s answer, with English quotation continuation preserved.

Two pages → overhearing maid → Patience → Xi-feng is intact; the initial uncertainty whether Wang-er was the rebuker survives until his admission. Outer and inner doorway positions, obedience and cold laughter carry the power relation.

Xi-feng’s sarcastic question is not logically corrected into a sincere one. Wang-er admits silencing Joker and Xi-er but denies inside knowledge; Xi-feng’s collective abuse and order to fetch Joker remain allegations and threats.
Joker begins in the accounts office, frightened by the summons without yet guessing its cause. Wang-er announces him; Xi-feng’s harsh voice and opening irony progressively strip his composure.

Xi-feng alternates a claimed exculpation, promise of leniency and threat over false words. Joker’s trembling question provokes her shouted face-slapping command. These are her tactics, not guarantees of safety.

Wang-er is stopped before striking; Joker hits his own cheeks repeatedly, removes his cap and knocks on the brick floor. His report separates the Ning funeral departure, Yu Lu’s collection trip and Lian/Rong’s talk about two sisters.

Singular praise is defensible and corroborated by complete 64.46, where Er-jie is specifically praised. Second Aunt preserves the socially dangerous address that Xi-feng rejects. Repaired 瞅 is a glance, not a sound; Joker asks permission to continue.

Xi-feng’s coarse maternal expletive, contempt for asking pardon, Joker’s partial denial and her faint cold smile retain their force. The unusual literal insult is a deliberate register choice, not a modern clinical or moral gloss.

House behind the mansion, Patience’s silence, silver reportedly given without an amount, the Zhang/Li-family idiom and Joker’s Second Mistress slip survive. He slaps himself; laughter is involuntary/exasperated, not reconciliation.

Joker’s early betrothal, poverty, promised silver and withdrawal account remain reported. Xi-feng notices his inconsistent claimed ignorance. House papering, marriage and her question where the bride came from are present; no document inquiry is inserted.

Mother’s house, Rong and attendants, You-shi’s visit after two days, praise, service and co-residents remain. The third-person business-pretext reading is defensible against complete 64.43 and 65.26, so a forced second-person correction was rejected.

San-jie’s death yesterday is Joker’s account; Xi-feng’s cuckold judgment stays hers. His oath and her conditional broken-leg threat do not become punishments carried out. Repaired 磕 leads into rising and retreat to the outer doorway.

Repeated recall and dismissal, the ban on visits, immediate attendance order and sarcastic invitation to tell Jia Lian all preserve coercive control. Joker does not receive actual permission to disclose.
Xi-feng, not Wang-er, performs the silent scrutiny, lasting two/three utterances. Both confidentiality threats remain hers. Wang-er assents and leaves; no later action is imported.
The tea request cues the maids’ withdrawal, leaving Patience’s silent smile. Xi-feng’s increasing anger and sudden plan are explicit narrative facts, but the plan’s content remains withheld.
Patience answers the summons; Xi-feng decides not to wait for Jia Lian. The exact local suspense close remains, with no chapter-68 itinerary or expanded resolution.

Er-jie was startled too, but the visitor was already there, and there was nothing to do but receive her courteously. She hastily straightened her clothes and came out to meet her. As she reached the gate, Xi-feng was just alighting from the carriage. All the ornaments in her hair were plain white silver. She wore a pale-blue satin jacket, a dark satin cloak and a plain skirt of white damask. Her brows curved like willow leaves, their tips lifted high; her long phoenix eyes held a keen, triangular glint. She was as lovely as peach blossom in spring, as pure and fresh as chrysanthemums in autumn. Zhou Rui's wife and Wang-er's wife supported her into the courtyard. Er-jie hurried forward, smiling, to make her greeting.
‘Sister, you honour me with your visit. Forgive me for not coming farther to meet you, and for receiving you so unprepared.’
She sank into a curtsey. Xi-feng hastened to return her smile and her salutations, and the two went indoors hand in hand.

‘I am young, and everything to do with my coming here was discussed and decided by my mother and elder sister. You and I are alike in our foolish devotion, but Master Lian has misunderstood me. He might perhaps conceal his visits to those places, but marrying you as a secondary wife is a great event, a solemn family ceremony, and even of that he told me nothing. I myself have urged him to take this step early, so that he might have children.
